title: Harbor Adapters and Harbor-Index: Infrastructure and a Curated Meta-Dataset for Large-Scale Agentic Evaluation
abstract: Evaluating agents on the growing number of agentic benchmarks is challenging because they often require complex environments and agent integrations. We introduce Harbor Adapters, a unified evaluation infrastructure for agentic benchmarks. Our work makes three contributions. First, we develop benchmark adapters that port more than 80 benchmarks to evaluate arbitrary agents, and validate them through rigorous code review and parity experiments. Second, we conduct a large-scale evaluation of 8 models spanning capability tiers across 54 benchmarks; every model is run with Terminus-2 and with one of 3 native harnesses. This enables a broader analysis of agent capabilities and failure modes than was previously possible. Third, we introduce Harbor-Index, a curated set of 82 difficult, diverse, and high-quality tasks spanning 29 benchmarks, refined from the adapted suite through difficulty filtering, AI and human audit, and an audit-and-fix loop. Harbor-Index preserves the challenge and breadth of large-scale agentic evaluations while being affordable to run; no evaluated model-harness configuration exceeds 30% pass rate, and the strongest (GPT-5.5 with Codex) reaches 28.0%. We release the adapters, evaluation results, in-depth analysis, and Harbor-Index as open-source artifacts to support more reliable and comprehensive evaluation of language-model agents.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Welcome to Advanced Topics in AI Evaluation. Today's lecture is on 'Harbor Adapters and Harbor-Index: Infrastructure and a Curated Meta-Dataset for Large-Scale Agentic Evaluation.' We've seen a surge in evaluation frameworks recently, like AgentBench and the Holistic Agent Leaderboard, all trying to standardize how we assess LLM agents. This work, from a large collaboration including researchers at Cornell Tech and Stanford, tackles the infrastructure problem head-on. As agentic systems get more complex, the evaluation landscape has become incredibly fragmented, which this paper argues is a major bottleneck for progress. Go ahead, Noah?
segments.zh: 欢迎来到AI评估高级专题。今天的讲座主题是“Harbor适配器与Harbor-Index：面向大规模智能体评估的基础设施与精选元数据集”。最近我们看到了评估框架的大量涌现，比如AgentBench和整体智能体排行榜，它们都在试图标准化我们评估LLM智能体的方式。这项工作来自一个大型合作团队，包括康奈尔科技和斯坦福的研究人员，直接正面解决了基础设施问题。随着智能体系统变得越来越复杂，评估领域已经变得极其碎片化，而这篇论文认为这是阻碍进展的一大瓶颈。诺亚，请讲？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Excuse me, Professor. The report mentions this fragmentation leads to an O(mn) integration problem. Could you explain what that means?
segments.zh: 不好意思，教授。报告里提到这种碎片化会导致一个O(mn)的集成问题。您能解释一下这是什么意思吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Certainly. Imagine you have 'm' benchmarks and 'n' agents. In a fragmented ecosystem, to test every agent on every benchmark, you need to write custom integration code for each specific pair. This creates a multiplicative workload of 'm times n' integrations. It's inefficient and severely limits the scale of any evaluation.
segments.zh: 当然可以。想象一下，你有m个基准和n个智能体。在一个碎片化的生态里，要在每个基准上测试每个智能体，你就得为每一对组合写专门的集成代码。这就产生了m乘n的集成工作量，是乘法级的增长。这种做法效率很低，而且严重限制了任何评估的规模。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So the main idea is to fix that bottleneck.
segments.zh: 所以核心思路就是解决这个瓶颈。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Precisely. The paper has three core objectives. First, to create a unified infrastructure called 'Harbor Adapters.' These adapters act as a universal translator, converting diverse benchmark formats into a single, standardized schema. This changes the integration problem from O(mn) to O(m+n), because you only need to write one adapter per benchmark and one integration per agent. Second, they use this new infrastructure to conduct a massive, large-scale evaluation of eight major models across 54 benchmarks. This was previously infeasible. Finally, from this huge dataset, they distill a small, high-quality, and difficult meta-dataset called 'Harbor-Index' to facilitate more efficient and reliable future testing.
segments.zh: 没错。这篇论文有三个核心目标。第一，构建一个叫“Harbor Adapters”的统一基础设施。这些适配器就像一个通用翻译器，把各种不同的基准格式转换成单一、标准化的模式。这就把集成问题从O(mn)降到了O(m+n)，因为你只需要为每个基准写一个适配器，为每个智能体做一次集成。第二，他们用这个新基础设施，对八个主要模型在54个基准上做了一次大规模评估。这在以前是做不到的。最后，从这个庞大的数据集中，他们提炼出一个规模小、质量高、难度大的元数据集，叫“Harbor-Index”，用来支持未来更高效、更可靠的测试。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: A universal translator for benchmarks sounds powerful, but also prone to error. How did they ensure these adapters were faithful to the original benchmarks?
segments.zh: 为基准做通用翻译器听起来很强大，但也容易出错。他们是怎么确保这些适配器忠实于原始基准的？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: An excellent and critical question. They didn't just write the code; they implemented a rigorous, multi-stage validation process. First, each adapter went through automated checks and then a two-tiered human review process by junior and senior reviewers to ensure semantic fidelity. The key, however, was conducting 'parity experiments.' They would run the same agent with the exact same configuration on both the original benchmark and its Harbor-adapted version. Parity was considered successful if the performance scores agreed within their standard errors across multiple trials. This provides strong evidence that the adapters faithfully replicate the original benchmark's logic and environment.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常好且关键的问题。他们不只是写了代码，而是实施了一套严格的多阶段验证流程。首先，每个适配器都要经过自动化检查，然后由初级和高级评审人员进行两级人工审核，以确保语义上的忠实度。但关键在于进行“一致性实验”。他们会用完全相同的配置，在原始基准和经过 Harbor 适配的版本上运行同一个智能体。如果在多次试验中，性能分数在标准误差范围内一致，就认为一致性验证成功。这提供了强有力的证据，说明适配器忠实地复现了原始基准的逻辑和环境。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So what did they learn from running this huge evaluation once they had the infrastructure in place?
segments.zh: 那他们在基础设施就位之后，从这次大规模评估中得出了什么结论呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: A few key things. They found significant redundancy in the current benchmark landscape. A Principal Component Analysis on the results showed that a single shared 'capability factor' explained over 70% of the performance variation. In fact, they found that a carefully selected set of about 12 benchmarks could capture most of the unique signals from the full set of 54. This suggests we don't need hundreds of benchmarks to get a clear picture. They also quantified the influence of the base model versus the 'harness'—the code that orchestrates the agent's actions. Their linear mixed model analysis showed that the base model's capability is a much stronger driver of performance than the specifics of the harness design.
segments.zh: 有几个关键发现。他们发现当前的基准格局存在大量冗余。对结果做主成分分析后显示，单一共享的“能力因子”就能解释超过70%的性能差异。事实上，他们发现精心挑选的大约12个基准就能捕捉到全部54个基准中大部分独特信号。这说明我们不需要几百个基准就能看清全貌。他们还量化了基础模型与“框架”之间的影响——框架就是编排智能体行动的那套代码。他们的线性混合模型分析显示，基础模型的能力对性能的驱动作用远大于框架设计的具体细节。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: That model versus harness finding is interesting. It seems to contrast a bit with work like HarnessDev, which focuses on the agent's ability to evolve its own harness. Does this paper suggest harness development is less important?
segments.zh: 模型与工具框架的这个发现挺有意思。它似乎跟HarnessDev这类工作有点矛盾，后者关注的是智能体自我演化工具框架的能力。那这篇论文是不是在暗示工具框架的开发没那么重要？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Not necessarily less important, but perhaps secondary to the raw capability of the foundation model. The harness still has a statistically significant effect; for instance, native harnesses for models like GPT-4 and Claude often performed better than the general-purpose Terminus-2 harness. However, the performance gap between a model like GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 was far larger than the gap between any two harnesses on the same model. The harness can optimize performance, but the model sets the ceiling. Another key insight came from creating Harbor-Index. They found that about a third of the tasks that seemed difficult at first were actually just broken—they had ambiguous instructions, faulty verifiers, or broken environments. Real difficulty is distinct from structural flaws.
segments.zh: 不一定没那么重要，但可能次于基础模型的原始能力。框架仍然有统计上显著的影响；比如GPT-4和Claude这些模型的原生框架通常比通用的Terminus-2框架表现更好。然而，GPT-4和GPT-3.5之间的性能差距，远大于同一模型上任意两个框架之间的差距。框架可以优化性能，但模型决定了上限。另一个关键洞见来自构建Harbor-Index。他们发现，最初看起来困难的任务中，大约有三分之一其实是坏的——指令含糊、验证器有缺陷，或者环境损坏。真正的难度和结构性缺陷是两回事。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So the implication is that we're often testing agents on flawed tasks, which might not reflect their true capabilities.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着我们经常用有缺陷的任务去测试智能体，这可能无法反映它们真正的能力。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. This work shifts the conversation from simply creating more benchmarks to focusing on the quality, validity, and efficiency of our evaluations. By providing the Harbor Adapters, they're not just offering a new leaderboard; they're offering a standardized, scalable infrastructure that enables more reliable and comparable science. The curated Harbor-Index serves as a proof of concept—a smaller, cheaper, but more challenging and trustworthy benchmark that filters out the noise of flawed tasks. It pushes the field toward more rigorous and meaningful evaluation.
segments.zh: 确实如此。这项工作把讨论的焦点从单纯创建更多基准，转向关注评估的质量、有效性和效率。通过提供 Harbor Adapters，他们不只是推出了一个新的排行榜，而是提供了一套标准化、可扩展的基础设施，让科学研究更可靠、更具可比性。精心筛选的 Harbor-Index 则是一个概念验证——一个规模更小、成本更低，但更具挑战性也更值得信赖的基准，能够过滤掉有缺陷任务带来的噪声。它推动整个领域走向更严谨、更有意义的评估。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: So, the big takeaway here is the move from quantity to quality in agent evaluation. This paper provides both the infrastructure to manage the current sprawling landscape and a methodology to curate it into something more focused and reliable. It’s a call for building better, not just more, yardsticks to measure agent progress. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 所以，这里最核心的要点是：智能体评估正在从追求数量转向追求质量。这篇论文既提供了管理当前庞杂格局的基础设施，也给出了一套方法论，把它整理成更聚焦、更可靠的东西。这是在呼吁我们打造更好的衡量标准，而不只是更多的标准，来衡量智能体的进展。感谢收听。如果还有任何问题，可以问我们的人工智能助手，或者留言评论。
